issues.body: `_measurement_stem()` claims an injective rendering, but its non-plain branch combines a lossy slug with only the first 12 hex characters of SHA-256. Distinct complete subject terms with the same slug can share that 48-bit prefix, producing the same measurement resource and recreating the multiple-`dqv:computedOn`/conflicting-`dqv:value` corruption from round 1. The new test checks a few examples, not the claimed invariant.
issues.fix_hint: Use a genuinely reversible Turtle-safe encoding of the complete subject term, or include the full cryptographic digest and describe the identity as collision-resistant rather than injective. If exact injectivity is required by the data model, prefer reversible encoding. Update the docstrings/tests so they assert the property actually provided.
issues.title: Truncated digest does not make measurement IRI minting injective

verdict.summary: Round 2 addresses the obvious cross-prefix collision and adds a useful regression test, but the promised injective identity is still not achieved. Non-plain subjects are distinguished only by a 12-hex-character (48-bit) truncated SHA-256 digest after a lossy slug, so distinct accepted subject terms can still mint the same measurement IRI and silently merge measurements. Because the prior major graph-corruption class remains, progress is stagnant.
